note: Adapted from the species description of Adaiphrotermes scapheutes by Sands (1972), originally in English; the species has no soldier, and the alate is known only from queen specimens, whose colour the original already noted as possibly faded; measurement-table headings, figure numbers and locality records are not translated, and some measurement values corrupted by OCR in the tables are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The range of this species possibly overlaps that of A. choanensis; the alate differs from it in the wavy posterior margin of the postclypeus and the indistinct fontanelle; the worker has different mandibles and a more strongly inflated fore tibia. Comparison with A. cuniculator is given in the discussion of that species.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule straw yellow, pilosity fine, short and fairly abundant, yellow. Postclypeus rather weakly inflated, Pcl/Rj 1.59, Pcl/W 0.21; proximal end of left accessory marginal tooth separated from the molar prominence by a distinct notch. Fore tibia strongly inflated, T1/Tw 3.08. Mixed segment long, 5–6 times the width of the midgut at the insertion of the Malpighian tubules; enteric valve seat with three distinct equal lobes and a short neck connecting to the second hindgut pouch; internal cushions entirely reticulate, membrane beyond the cushions with reduced spines.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Known only from the queen, the colour possibly faded; head capsule yellowish brown, brown above the ocelli; fontanelle almost absent, very small, oval, flat, brown; middle spot larger than the fontanelle, one third the diameter of an ocellus, flat, yellowish brown; postclypeus pale yellowish brown, labrum yellow; frontal mark an indistinct crescent, flat, pale yellowish brown; antennae yellow. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum pale yellowish brown, mesothoracic suture absent, metathoracic suture present; legs, femora and tibiae yellow, tarsi yellowish white. Abdominal tergites pale yellowish brown, dorsolateral spiracles darker, yellowish brown; sternites yellow laterally and paler medially, ventrolateral spiracles pale yellowish brown, cerci yellowish white. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli medium-sized, separated from the compound eye by two thirds their own minimum diameter; postclypeus rather large, rather strongly inflated, Pcl/W index 0.32, posterior margin wavy and not evenly rounded, median suture weak. Head capsule pilosity uneven, not forming a felt, yellow.
